title: Ben Zakkai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Mishnah Sanhedrin 5:2: “An incident — Ben Zakkai examined the stems of figs.” In the Gemara there, 41a, the Gemara first supposes that this is not Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and in the end concludes that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was then a student sitting before his teacher, and they called him Ben Zakkai; afterward, when he taught, they called him Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

There is also a Ben Zakkai who was an Amora, as in Chullin 53a: “Ulla said: Ben Zakkai said … Rabbi Yochanan said”; but Hyman reports Tosafot’s reading there as “Ulla ben Zakkai.” In Semachot, chapter 8: an incident with Yehudah and Hillel, the sons of Rabban Gamliel (son of Rabbi), who went in to Ben Zakkai in Babylonia; Hyman calls this a scribal error and proposes “to Rabbi Zakkai in Kabul.”

notes.text: Hyman proposes changing Ben Zakkai in Babylonia to Rabbi Zakkai in Kabul; this is an attributed emendation, not an independently established place or genealogy. The supplied בר רבי and Ulla/Ben Zakkai alternatives remain visible.

The supplied Chullin 53a is preserved. The directly matching consulted Bavli passage is Chullin 52a, with Ulla reporting Ben Zakkai and a separate Rabbi Yochanan opinion. Tosafot there has עולא בר רבי זכאי, a patronymic form distinct from the Bavli punctuation and Hyman’s supplied ben form. Tractate Semachot 8 directly has Yehudah and Hillel, sons of Rabban Gamliel, visiting Ben Zakkai in Babylonia. Kabul/Rabbi Zakkai and the parenthetical son-of-Rabbi remain Hyman’s emendation and genealogy, not new admissions.
